name: Asa
bio:
Asa was Abijam's son, who succeeded him as king of Judah and reigned forty-one years in Jerusalem (1 Kings 15:8-10). Unlike his father and grandfather, Asa did what was right in the LORD's eyes, as David had: he expelled the shrine prostitutes from the land, removed the idols his predecessors had made, and even deposed his own grandmother Maachah from her position as queen mother because she had made a detestable Asherah pole, which Asa cut down and burned in the Kidron Valley. Though the high places were not removed, "Asa's heart was fully committed to the LORD all his life," and he brought the silver, gold, and articles he and his father had dedicated into the temple (1 Kings 15:11-15).

There was war between Asa and Baasha, king of Israel, throughout their reigns. When Baasha fortified Ramah to blockade Judah, cutting off all movement to and from Jerusalem, Asa emptied the treasuries of the temple and palace and sent the silver and gold to Ben-Hadad, king of Aram in Damascus, to persuade him to break his treaty with Baasha and attack Israel instead. Ben-Hadad agreed, attacking several of Israel's northern cities, which forced Baasha to abandon his fortification of Ramah; Asa then had all Judah carry away the stone and timber Baasha had used and used it to fortify Geba and Mizpah instead (1 Kings 15:16-22). Asa suffered from a disease in his feet in his old age. When he died, he was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, and his son Jehoshaphat succeeded him (1 Kings 15:23-24).
